faqs.q: Sec. 58-10. - Motions of defense or objections based on defects in prosecution or form of summonses or complaints.
faqs.a:
(a)
Defenses and objections based on defects in the institution of the prosecution or
               the form of the summons or complaint or both other than failure to show jurisdiction
               in the court or to charge an offense may be raised only by motion. The motion shall
               include all such defenses and objections then available to the defendant. Failure
               thus to present any such defense or objection constitutes a waiver of it, but the
               court for cause shown may grant relief from the waiver.
(b)
Such motion shall be made before the plea is entered, but the court may permit it
               to be made within a reasonable time thereafter. Motions under this section shall be
               determined before trial unless the court orders that it be deferred for determination
               at the trial of the general issue.
(c)
If a motion is determined adversely to the defendant, he shall be permitted to plead
               if he has not previously pleaded. A plea previously entered shall stand.
(Code 1960, § 1-25; Code 1981, § 18-14)
